=== NOTES 5:121 | Disease-specific Programmes – Tb, Malaria, Hiv/aids, Ncd and Mental Health
## SUB 0 | HIV/AIDS – Facts, Tests, Drugs and Programmes
[121:0:0] - **HIV causes AIDS**; first recognised **1981**; dominant strain in India **HIV-1 subtype C**.
[121:0:1] - **Transmission**: sexual contact, **blood transfusion**/needles, **mother to child across the placenta** (and breastfeeding) – **not by mosquitoes or other blood-sucking insects**.
[121:0:2] - **Symptoms of AIDS**: swollen lymph nodes, night sweats, weight loss, and neurological problems incl. **memory loss** – all four of the classic PYQ list.
[121:0:3] - **ELISA** = first widely used HIV screening test (detects antibodies); **Zidovudine (Azidothymidine, AZT)** = the most used anti-retroviral. No licensed HIV vaccine.
[121:0:4] TABLE head: Programme / term | Fact
  [121:0:4.0] NACP (NACO, MoHFW) | Launched 1992; Phase V 2021–26 (80% cut in new infections and deaths)
  [121:0:4.1] VCTC | Voluntary Counselling and Testing Centre (now ICTC – Integrated Counselling and Testing Centre)
  [121:0:4.2] 'Test and Treat' (2017) | Every HIV-positive person gets free ART regardless of CD4 count
  [121:0:4.3] Project Sunrise (2016) | HIV/AIDS among people who inject drugs in the North-Eastern States
  [121:0:4.4] HIV/AIDS Act 2017 | Bars discrimination against people living with HIV
  [121:0:4.5] Red Ribbon Express / AVAHAN | Awareness train / Gates Foundation prevention initiative
[121:0:5] - **Sub-Saharan Africa** = region with the most HIV/AIDS cases (UNAIDS 2003 and since); UNAIDS set up 1996; 95-95-95 target.
[121:0:6] - **15th International AIDS Conference**, Bangkok, July 2004 – slogan **"Access for All"**.
[121:0:7] - India: highest burden Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka. World AIDS Day 1 December.
[121:0:8] ~~ Sources: NextGen Rocket Biology p.24 (AIDS transmission), p.32 (no HIV vaccine), p.33 (Zidovudine/AZT); app notes; general knowledge, not checked (Bangkok slogan, Project Sunrise, Test and Treat)
[121:0:9] - 2026: UNAIDS 'United to end AIDS' report released at the **26th International AIDS Conference, Rio de Janeiro**.
[121:0:10] - NACP phases: I 1992–99; II 1999–2006; III 2007–12; IV 2012–17 (extended to 2021); V 2021–26.
[121:0:11] - **95-95-95** (UNAIDS): know status → on treatment → **viral load suppressed**.
## SUB 1 | Eradication and Certification Milestones – Smallpox, Polio, Yaws
[121:1:0] TABLE head: Milestone | Year
  [121:1:0.0] Smallpox eradicated worldwide (only human disease eradicated) | 1980 (India free 1977)
  [121:1:0.1] Pulse Polio – OPV to all children under five (Dec and Jan rounds) | 1995
  [121:1:0.2] Guinea worm (dracunculiasis) – India certified free | 2000 (not eradicated worldwide)
  [121:1:0.3] Last wild polio case (Howrah) | Jan 2011
  [121:1:0.4] Rinderpest (cattle plague) eradicated worldwide | 2011 (2nd disease ever)
  [121:1:0.5] WHO South-East Asia Region polio-free | 27 March 2014
  [121:1:0.6] Yaws – India certified free | 2016
  [121:1:0.7] Trivalent → bivalent OPV (types 1 and 3) | April 2016
[121:1:1] - **Jonas Salk** – first (injected, inactivated) **polio** vaccine (1955); **Albert Sabin** – oral polio vaccine; **Edward Jenner** – smallpox vaccine (1796).
[121:1:2] - **Diphtheria and chickenpox are NOT eradicated** – of the UPSC 2014 list only **smallpox**.
[121:1:3] ~~ Sources: NextGen Rocket Biology p.3, p.18, p.32 (Salk, Sabin, OPV types), p.37 (rinderpest 2011); PMF Science & Technology Part 3 p.44 (smallpox 1980); app notes
## SUB 2 | Tuberculosis – NTEP, Ni-kshay and TB Reports
[121:2:0] - India topped the world in new TB cases (WHO, **2016** and since); TB is the **leading single infectious killer** (WHO).
[121:2:1] - National target: TB elimination **2025** (SDG 2030). **BCG** protects against TB.
[121:2:2] TABLE head: Scheme / term | Feature
  [121:2:2.0] Ni-kshay | Central TB Division's web-enabled patient management system (notification, tracking)
  [121:2:2.1] Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana (2018) | Nutritional DBT for the whole duration of anti-TB treatment – ₹500/month, raised to ₹1,000 from Oct 2024
  [121:2:2.2] PM TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (Sep 2022) | Ni-kshay Mitras adopt patients
  [121:2:2.3] India TB Report 2022 | Notifications in 2021 up 19% over 2020
  [121:2:2.4] India TB Report 2024 | Estimated incidence 2023 ≈ 27–28 lakh (between 25 and 30 lakh); 25.52 lakh notified
  [121:2:2.5] WHO Global TB Report 2025 | India incidence 237 → 187 per lakh (-21%), 2015–2024; mortality 28 → 21 per lakh (-25%); treatment coverage 53% → 92%; 26.18 lakh diagnosed of ~27 lakh
[121:2:3] - World TB Day 24 March. AP notified over 78,000 cases in 2024.
[121:2:4] ~~ Sources: Rocket CA 2026 Part 02 p.112-113 (Global TB Report 2025); MoHFW press release 7783, 7 Oct 2024 (Ni-kshay Poshan ₹1,000; search result); app notes
[121:2:5] - TB campaign since Dec 2024: **20 crore+ screened**, 28 lakh+ diagnosed (Aug 2026).
[121:2:6] - TB **treatment success rate**: 83% (2021) → **90% (2025)**.
## SUB 3 | Malaria – Elimination, Quinine and Vaccines
[121:3:0] - **National Framework for Malaria Elimination 2016–2030**: zero indigenous cases by **2027**, elimination by **2030**. **MERA India** (ICMR) supports the 2030 goal.
[121:3:1] - **Quinine** comes from the **bark of Cinchona**.
[121:3:2] - Vaccines: **RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix, GSK)** – first; **R21/Matrix-M** – **Oxford Jenner Institute + Serum Institute of India** (Novavax adjuvant); AdFalciVax – ICMR-RMRC Bhubaneswar candidate.
[121:3:3] - NVBDCP tools: IRS, LLINs, larvivorous fish, source reduction (not antibiotic prophylaxis). WHO malaria-free: Maldives (first in SEAR), Sri Lanka (2016), China, Timor-Leste.
[121:3:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen Rocket Biology p.32 (malaria vaccines), p.33 (quinine), p.75 (Cinchona bark); Rocket CA 2026 Part 02 p.111-112 (targets 2027/2030); app notes
[121:3:5] - NVBDCP covers outbreaks of **malaria, dengue and chikungunya** (and JE, kala-azar, LF).
[121:3:6] - Malaria cases fell about **80%** in India (2015–2023).
## SUB 4 | Vaccines in News – HPV/Cervavac, Hib and Serum Institute
[121:4:0] - **Cervavac** (Sep 2022): India's **first indigenous quadrivalent HPV vaccine** against **cervical cancer** – **Serum Institute of India** with **DBT-BIRAC** (not Indian Immunologicals).
[121:4:1] - India carries about **one-fifth of the global cervical-cancer burden** (~1.23 lakh cases, ~67,000 deaths a year).
[121:4:2] - Nationwide free **HPV vaccination** for 14-year-old girls: launched **28 Feb 2026, Ajmer** (single dose).
[121:4:3] - **Serum Institute of India** is in **Pune** (Hib, MR, Covishield, R21).
[121:4:4] TABLE head: Disease | Vaccine
  [121:4:4.0] Rubella | MMR
  [121:4:4.1] Tetanus | DTP
  [121:4:4.2] Tuberculosis | BCG
[121:4:5] ~~ Sources: Rocket CA 2026 Part 02 p.110 (HPV campaign); NextGen Rocket Biology p.32 (BCG, DPT); app notes; general knowledge, not checked (Cervavac partners, Pune)
[121:4:6] - **Shanvac-B** – India's first genetically engineered vaccine (**hepatitis B**); **ZyCoV-D** – DNA-based COVID-19 vaccine.
[121:4:7] - **Diphtheria** is prevented by a **toxoid** vaccine (part of DPT).
## SUB 5 | Sickle Cell, Leprosy and Other Elimination Missions
[121:5:0] - **Sickle cell anaemia**: a **congenital, inherited** single-gene disorder (haemoglobin) – misshapen red cells cannot carry oxygen properly. **National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission**: launched **1 July 2023, Shahdol (MP)**; eliminate by **2047**; screen **7 crore** at-risk (tribal) people.
[121:5:1] - **Leprosy**: NLEP gives free MDT; **World Leprosy Day = last Sunday of January**; Anti-Leprosy Day (India) **30 January**.
[121:5:2] - Lymphatic filariasis 2027 (IDA = Ivermectin, DEC, Albendazole); measles-rubella 2026; kala-azar target met 2023.
[121:5:3] - **Elimination targets**: TB 2025, measles-rubella 2026, lymphatic filariasis 2027, malaria 2030, AIDS as a public health threat 2030, sickle cell 2047. **IDSP** (2004, under NHM) = outbreak surveillance, not an NCD target.
[121:5:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen Rocket Biology p.34 (sickle cell – inherited); app notes
[121:5:5] - **Sparsh** Leprosy Awareness Campaign (from 30 January).

## SUB 7 | Mental Health

  [121:7:0.1] Mental Health Act | 1987 | Repealed 2017
  [121:7:0.2] Mental Healthcare Act (Bill 2016) | 2017 | Right to access care; advance directives; access to records; decriminalised suicide; ECT for minors prohibited in the Bill (Act: only with guardian consent and Board permission); no ECT without anaesthesia
  [121:7:0.3] Tele-MANAS | 2022 | 24/7 tele-mental health
[121:7:1] - **Eating disorders** (anorexia, bulimia) usually begin in **adolescence**.
[121:7:2] - Burden about 1 in 7 Indians; treatment gap 84.5%.
[121:7:3] ~~ Sources: app notes; general knowledge, not checked (ECT clause, eating disorders)
## SUB 8 | NCDs, Tobacco and Physical Activity
[121:8:0] - **NP-NCD** (earlier NPCDCS): population-based screening. India Hypertension Control Initiative (ICMR) – heart attack, stroke, kidney failure.
[121:8:1] - **E-cigarettes**: about **12 States** had banned them before the national **Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes Act 2019**.
[121:8:2] - **Milkha Singh** – WHO Goodwill Ambassador for **physical activity**, South-East Asia Region (2018).
[121:8:3] - AP: expanded NP-NCD also covers mental health, elderly care, IDD, tobacco, fluorosis, oral health.
